answer.rationale: Incumbent has refused price movement and the line runs at 94% with no buffer, so a full primary switch (per memory_c2's cost win) carries unverified delivery risk this close to expiry. Adding a second source (memory_c3) de-risks the single point of failure, creates competitive leverage for the 18% mandate, and can be scoped as a guarded partial allocation rather than a wholesale migration. Before committing, I want to verify memory_c2 (was the low-cost vendor's quick onboarding validated under load, and at what volumes?) and memory_c3 (did dual-sourcing actually hold allocation, and what were onboarding timelines/costs?). If verification shows the low-cost vendor has proven capacity at our volume, a staged shift of share toward them within the second-source framework can deliver much of the cost cut without a single-cycle cliff-edge migration.
